title: Find All Occurrences of a Pattern
real_world_story: A document-analysis system needs to locate every occurrence of a keyword or phrase inside a large document. The search should avoid repeatedly comparing characters that have already been matched.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: KMP pattern matching using a prefix table to search efficiently

problem_statement: Given a text string and a pattern string, find all starting indices where the pattern occurs in the text. Print the indices in increasing order. If the pattern does not occur, print -1.
task: Use the KMP pattern-matching algorithm to locate every occurrence of the pattern, including overlapping occurrences.
input_format: The first line contains the text string. The second line contains the pattern string.
output_format: Print all zero-based starting indices separated by spaces. If there is no occurrence, print -1.
constraints: Text and pattern contain lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: The pattern occurs at indices 0, 1, and 2, including overlapping occurrences.

expected_algorithm.name: KMP Pattern Matching
expected_algorithm.reason: KMP preprocesses the pattern and avoids unnecessary re-comparisons, making it suitable for large text searches.

hint: Build the LPS/prefix table for the pattern.
Scan the text using the pattern index.
When a mismatch occurs, use the LPS value instead of restarting from the beginning.
Record every complete match and continue searching for overlaps.
real_world_takeaway: Efficient pattern matching is important when search systems process large documents, logs, source files, or repeated keyword queries.
